bugs.text: px() takes a single string, so the second frame passed for zako and goei is dropped and every SPR entry is an array of row strings; drawSprite does sp[frame].map on a string and throws 'g.map is not a function' the first time the title score table is drawn. The exception happens before requestAnimationFrame(frame) is re-requested, so the page freezes after a partial first frame (GALAGA / NAMCO 1981, static stars). Confirmed by result.json pageerror and all screenshots being the same title frame.
updateShots, updateEBullets, updateExplosions and updateGameOver use dt, which is not a parameter or global: ReferenceError on the first update after Enter even if the sprite bug were fixed.
clamp01 is called but never defined; entryPathPoint would throw if anything called it (nothing does, so entering enemies would also never follow a path).

newFormation creates 40 'zako' only; no Boss Galaga or Goei ever exist, so buildEntryGroups pushes undefined into each group (forEach at 204 would throw on e.state), and dives, escorts, tractor beam and capture can never occur.
checkStageClear is an empty placeholder: a cleared stage never advances.

Challenging stage: startChallenging never changes G.state and updateChallenge is never called, so the stageIntro branch re-calls startChallenging every frame (8 new enemies per frame) and the stage can never finish.
killPlayer clamps reserve to 0 and then tests reserve<0, so endGame is unreachable from losing ships: the player respawns forever.
freeCaptured nulls G.captured before updateFreed checks G.captured.free; the rescue and dual-fighter docking can never happen.
Title score table prints the literal '50 / 100' for all three enemy rows instead of r[2].
Boss Galaga has a single sprite frame; frame index 1 would read undefined.
A Boss destroyed in formation scores 400 (+escort bonus) instead of 150.
Formation enemies are positioned once in enterFormation and never re-read slotPos, so sway and breathing would not move the formation.
A diver that leaves the bottom is teleported to its slot rather than re-entering from the top.
Stage badges are one flag per stage with labels 1-9, not the arcade 1/5/10/20/30/50 denominations, capped at 9 flags.
No READY text on respawn; no results (shots/hits/ratio) screen at game over despite stats being tracked (237, 262).
killPlayer calls drawExplosion() with no arguments from update logic, drawing NaN strokes outside render.
No edge detection on Space: holding fire spawns a shot every frame up to the two-shot cap.

summary: The file is laid out like a real Galaga clone, with named sections, a 224x288 integer-scaled canvas, an accumulator loop, a synthesized sound bank, pixel-art sprite strings, entry groups, bezier dives, a tractor-beam state machine, capture/rescue bookkeeping and challenging-stage scoring, but almost none of it was ever run: a one-argument sprite helper collapses the animation frames into row strings, so the very first render throws inside the title score table and the requestAnimationFrame chain dies, leaving a static 'GALAGA / NAMCO 1981' screen (result.json: loads_clean false, starts false, moves false). Behind that first crash sit several more fatal ones (undefined dt in four update functions, undefined clamp01, a formation that contains only Zako, an empty placeholder for stage clear, a challenging-stage branch that re-spawns waves every frame, a reserve-count check that makes game over unreachable, and a rescue path that nulls the captive before checking it). Code quality is uneven: readable names and section comments coexist with dead expressions (&&false, ||true), a monkey-patched update, and a hard-coded score table. It reads as a plausible sketch of Galaga that was never opened in a browser, and in its delivered state it is not playable.
